body:
# Ledger guests: tracking money of people without an account (design of record)

Decided with the maintainer on 2026-10-31. A ledger can hold **guests**: participants who have
no account on this server. A guest exists on exactly one ledger, is created and renamed by any
member, takes part in entries like a member, can be **locked** (the freeze without a vote), and
can later be **claimed** by a member, so the guest's history becomes that member's. This is
the contract the server, the web client and the Android client all implement; when it and the
code disagree, the code is wrong.

## 1. What a guest is

* A guest belongs to **one ledger** (`kind = expenses`). Nothing about a guest is visible from,
  or usable on, any other list; there is no server-wide guest registry. Shopping and checklist
  lists have no guests (served as `[]`).
* A guest has an **id** and a **name**. The id is server-minted, `g:` + uuid4, so no guest id
  is ever an account id and both clients tell the two apart by the prefix without a lookup
  (`ID_MAX_LENGTH` in `sync.py` already covers the length). The name is free text, 1..64
  characters after the server-message trim rules (`shared-test-cases/server-message.json`,
  step 1: trim tab/CR/LF/space and every Zs; refuse Cc/Zl/Zp/Cs and the bidi overrides), not
  unique on the list — two "Dave" slots are two people; rename one.
* A guest has a **locked** flag. Locked means what "voted to close" means for a member: the
  guest's paid and owed amounts may not move while the list is open (section 4). Anyone on the
  list can set or clear it for any guest; it is a safeguard against accidental edits, not a
  permission.
* A guest may be **claimed** by a member (section 5): `claimed_by` is that account id, or null.
* Guests **never vote** and never count towards closing: a list closes when every current
  *member* has voted, exactly as today. A ledger can therefore close with an unsettled guest
  balance; the lock is the only protection a guest has, and that is deliberate.

## 2. Wire format

### Served: on the list object

Guests are **server-maintained state on the list object**, next to `members` and
`close_votes`, outside `fields`, never client-written through `/sync` (one creation-time
exception below):

```json
"guests": [
  {"id": "g:…", "name": "Dave", "initials": "DA", "locked": false,
   "claimed_by": null, "created_at": 1761900000000}
]
```

Oldest first, then by id. `initials` are resolved server-side from the name (the
`_default_initials` rule in `auth.py`, applied to the name instead of an email's local part),
so a badge needs no second lookup, as for a member. Every guest change — create, rename, lock,
unlock, remove, claim, unclaim — bumps the list's `change_seq` (`touch_list`), so it reaches
every device through the ordinary incremental sync even though no field value moved (the
T-152 mechanism). A client that sends `guests` on a pushed list row has it ignored, like
`members`.

### Endpoints

Guests go through their own endpoints, like votes and invites. Rationale: offline creation
through `/sync` would need a third row kind with per-field clocks; adding a guest is as rare
as inviting someone and happens while the group is together, so the endpoints are the cheaper
contract. An entry that names a guest *is* an ordinary item write and stays fully offline.

| Endpoint | Request body | Success response |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /lists/{id}/guests` | `{"name"}` | `201 {guest object}` |
| `PATCH /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}` | `{"name"?, "locked"?}` | `200 {guest object}` |
| `DELETE /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}` | — | `204` |
| `POST /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}/claim` | — | `200 {guest object}` |
| `DELETE /lists/{id}/guests/{gid}/claim` | — | `200 {guest object}` |

A `PATCH` with neither key, or a `locked` that is not a boolean, is `422 invalid_request`.
Errors, all after the usual `403 not_a_member` (uniform whether or not the list exists), in
this order of checks:

| Answer | When |
|---|---|
| `409 not_an_expenses_list` | any of them on another kind |
| `409 list_closed` | any of them on a closed list — the archive is read-only, guests included |
| `422 voted_to_close` with `row_id` (the list id) | any of them by a member with a close vote: a voter changes nothing, and a claim or unclaim moves the voter's own balance |
| `404 guest_not_found` | `gid` is not a guest of **this** list (a guest of another list is 404 here, never anything that reveals it exists) |
| `422 invalid_guest_name` with `field: "name"` | name blank after trimming, over 64 characters, or refused by the control-character rules |
| `409 guest_claimed` | `PATCH {"locked"}` or `POST …/claim` on a guest that is already claimed; `DELETE …/claim` by anyone but the claimant |
| `409 guest_in_use` | `DELETE` while any **live** entry on the list names the guest (section 3) |
| `422 participant_frozen` with `account_id` (the guest id) | `POST …/claim` on a locked guest |

Renaming a claimed guest stays allowed (the name is what the old entries show), and a claimed
guest cannot be locked or unlocked: the claimant's vote governs those numbers now. A `PATCH`
with only `name` on a claimed guest is fine.

### Entries

Every key in `paid_by` / `paid_for` is one of:

* a current member's account id, or
* the id of a guest of this list — **claimed or not**, or
* any id already present in the row's stored entry (unchanged: an entry naming someone who
  left, or a removed guest, stays editable).

That is the one change to `_check_expense_against_list` in `sync.py`; the shape rules are
untouched, and a transfer between a guest and a member, or two guests, is an ordinary transfer
(two different ids). A claimed guest is accepted in a new entry on purpose: the clients never
offer one, but an entry written offline before the claim landed must not be quarantined for
it, and the fold (section 6) accounts it correctly either way. The `invalid_expense` message
for an unknown participant is reworded to "a member or a guest of the list".

### Guests at list creation

The one place guest *names* travel through `/sync`: a list row that **creates** a ledger may
carry its first guests, so a ledger made offline (Android queues the creation) arrives with
its people and nobody has to open the list menu afterwards.

```json
{"id": "…", "fields": {"name": …, "kind": …, "currency": …}, "guest_names": ["Dave", "Eve"]}
```

* `guest_names` sits **outside `fields`**: it is not an LWW field and has no clock. The key is
  deliberately not `guests`, which is the served objects, so a typed client never has one key
  with two shapes.
* It is honoured only when the row creates the list (no stored row with that id) and the
  resulting kind is `expenses`; on any later push of the list, or on another kind, it is
  **ignored**, as a client-sent `members` is. Creating guests later is the endpoint's job.
* The server mints them in the creation's transaction, in the array's order (strictly
  increasing `created_at`, so the served order is the typed order), so the list's first sync
  already serves them under `guests`.
* It is an array of at most **50** strings; each follows the guest-name rule. Anything else —
  not an array, a non-string, a bad name, too many — is `422 invalid_guest_name` with `row_id`
  and `field: "guest_names"`, and nothing of the row is created. Blank names are the client's
  to drop before pushing, never the server's to skip.
* No parsing on the wire: a name may contain a comma.

### Server storage

A `guests` table: `id` PK, `list_id` FK to lists, `name`, `locked` INTEGER, `claimed_by` TEXT
NULL (no FK: like `last_touched_by`, it is history and must survive the account), `created_at`,
`created_by`. Index on `list_id`. GC deletes a list's guests with the list (before the list row,
as `close_votes`). Housekeeping gets `guests_list_missing` and `guests_on_non_expenses_list`
checks. Deleting an account leaves `claimed_by` untouched.

## 3. Removing a guest

`DELETE` is allowed only while no live entry on the list names the guest; otherwise
`409 guest_in_use`, and the client says to edit those entries first (the client can tell in
advance and disables the control with the reason). On success the row is hard-deleted. A
tombstoned entry that still names the id is not in the way: if such an entry is ever
un-deleted by a winning write, the "already present in the stored entry" rule admits it, and
the clients render the id as they already render a departed member (section 6). That is the
former-member path, so no new client state is needed for it.

## 4. The freeze, with guests

`is_frozen(id)` in `closing.py` becomes:

* an account id: has voted, or is not a current member — unchanged;
* an unclaimed guest id: `locked`, or not (any more) a guest of this list;
* a claimed guest id: whatever `is_frozen` says for the **claimant's account** — the guest's
  numbers are that member's now.

`check_write_against_freeze` is otherwise unchanged and keeps comparing amounts **per stored
key**, not per folded id: a write that moves an amount from a claimed guest's key to the
claimant's own key is refused while the claimant is frozen, even though the folded balance
would not move. That is conservative and simple; nobody has a reason to make such a write. A
new row is a change from zero, a deletion a change to zero, a type change touches everyone,
and only a write that would win LWW is checked. The error stays `422 participant_frozen` with
`row_id`, `field` and the frozen id in `account_id` (a guest id there; the key keeps its name
so no client parsing changes).

"A voter changes nothing" (`voted_to_close`) is unchanged and, per the table in section 2,
covers every guest endpoint.

## 5. Claiming

Joining through an invite is unchanged on the wire: `POST /invites/redeem` makes the caller a
member. The chooser is a **client** step right after a successful redeem of an `expenses` list
whose synced list object carries unclaimed guests: "Are you one of these?" — one button per
unclaimed guest, and "No, I'm new". Picking one calls `POST …/claim`; "No, I'm new" closes it.
The same action is offered on the list menu for every unclaimed guest ("This is me"), so
someone who dismissed the chooser, or a member who was already on the list when the slot was
created, can claim later. No invite is ever tied to a guest.

Claiming records `claimed_by` and bumps `change_seq`; **no stored entry is rewritten**.
Rewriting map keys inside items would fight field-level LWW and stale offline writes; the alias
avoids it. Both clients fold a claimed guest into the claimant (section 6).

An account may claim more than one guest on a list (two slots that were both Dave); the fold is
a plain map, so nothing special-cases it. A claim is reversible by the claimant alone while the
list is open (`DELETE …/claim`), which turns the alias back into a plain guest; after the list
closes it is final, like everything else on the archive.

A claim or unclaim is refused when the caller has voted (`voted_to_close`), and a claim when
the guest is locked (`participant_frozen`), since it moves the caller's balance by the guest's.
Leaving an open list stays impossible (`list_open`); when the claimant leaves a closed list or
deletes their account, the claim stays as history and the clients render the account the way
they already render a former member.

## 6. Arithmetic: the fold (both clients, identical)

Given the list's guests, `aliases = {guest.id: guest.claimed_by for each claimed guest}`.

`fold(entry, aliases)` returns a copy of the entry in which every key of `paid_by` and
`paid_for` is replaced by `aliases[key] ?? key`, **summing in cents** the amounts of keys that
land on the same id (an entry that names both a guest and, from before the claim, the
claimant). `type`, `date`, `equal_by`, `equal_for` are copied. A folded entry is never written;
it exists for arithmetic and display only, so a transfer that folds to one id on both sides is
fine — its effect is zero, which is correct: it was the claimant paying themself.

Every figure is computed on folded entries, by the **existing** functions unchanged:
`balancesFor`, `entryEffectCents`, `spentTotals` (unaffected by the fold, totals do not move),
`settle`, and the per-entry effect shown on rows. `participantIds` passed to `balancesFor` is
members ∪ unclaimed guests, so a guest with no entries yet shows a zero row like a member.

Correctness, case by case:

| Case | Fold | Result |
|---|---|---|
| unclaimed guest | identity | behaves exactly like a member; sum-to-zero holds |
| claimed guest | g → A | A's paid/share/settled absorb g's; the balance is A's true position |
| several guests claimed by one account | g1 → A, g2 → A | same; plain map |
| entry naming g and A on one side | amounts summed under A | one row for A, nothing lost |
| stored transfer g → A, after the claim | A → A | effect 0, settled unchanged |
| unclaim | alias gone | the stored entries were never touched, so the split is exact |
| claimant left (closed list) or deleted | g → A, A not a member | A is a former member; numbered once over effective ids |

Property tests on both clients: balances over folded entries sum to zero for any mix of the
three types and any alias map; `fold` with an empty map is the identity; `fold` is idempotent.

**Frozen participants in the form** (the T-196 trap: an equal split must not zero a frozen
share) are computed on **stored keys**, mirroring the server: an account id is frozen when it
has voted or is not a member; an unclaimed guest when locked or not in `guests`; a claimed
guest when its claimant is frozen. The reason shown is the matching one: "agreed to close",
"no longer a member", "locked", or the claimant's reason.

**Former-member numbering** (T-197) runs over effective ids: `formerMemberNumbers` is fed
folded entries and the set of current members ∪ guests (claimed or not), so a removed guest
and a departed claimant each get one number, and a live claimed guest never does.

## 7. Shared cases

`shared-test-cases/expense-arithmetic.json` gains an optional `aliases` map on `balances` and
`effect` cases, applied through `fold` before the computation, with cases for: an unclaimed
guest among members; a claimed guest; two guests claimed by one account; an entry naming guest
and claimant on one side; a transfer that folds onto one id; and a settle case whose balances
include a guest id. Both clients run them; the sum-to-zero property test runs over alias maps
too.

## 8. Clients, both alike

**Labelling a participant id** (one function per client, used by every screen):

| id is | label | badge |
|---|---|---|
| a current member | as today (initials badge, email/you) | filled |
| an unclaimed guest | the guest's name | outline badge with the guest's initials; "guest" in the accessible label |
| a claimed guest (a stored key) | the guest's name, then the claimant's label — "Dave · DP" | the claimant's badge |
| none of those | "Former member N" exactly as today | as today |

**List menu** (web `ListPropsPage`, Android `ListPropsScreen`) gains a **Guests** section
directly under Members, on ledgers only:

* one row per guest: outline badge, name, and — on an open list — Rename (inline), a
  "Amounts locked" switch with the help line "Locked: the amounts cannot change, like a member
  who agreed to close", "This is me" while unclaimed, and Remove (disabled with "Named in
  entries — edit those first" while any live entry names the guest). A claimed guest shows
  "claimed by DP" instead of the switch and the claim button, and Unclaim for the claimant.
* an "Add guest" name field with an Add button, like "Invite by email".
* on a closed list the section is read-only, like the vote line.
* every control is also disabled with the voted-to-close hint while the viewer has voted,
  as the entry form is today.

**Create-list dialog** (web `OverviewPage`, Android's create dialog): when the kind is Ledger,
a **Guests** section under the currency — one name box, an "Add another" button that appends a
box, a remove control on each, "Add another" hidden at 50. Blank boxes are dropped on create;
the names go on the creation row's `guest_names`. No comma splitting. The section is hidden
for other kinds and against a server below the protocol version in section 9 (the key would
be ignored there, and the person would wonder where their guests went).

**Entry form** offers members and unclaimed guests as participants (claimed guests never), in
the roster order members-then-guests, guests with the outline badge; a locked guest is shown
as a voter is today (amount fixed, unselectable on a new entry, `frozenFreeSelection`).
Transfers may name a guest on either side.

**Entry rows** label stored keys with the table above; the per-entry effect is for the
viewer's *effective* id.

**Balances** show one row per effective id: members, unclaimed guests (marked), then former
ids; a locked guest carries an "amounts locked" line, worded apart from T-203's "agreed to
close" (a separate string on both clients). Settle-up lists guests like members; "Reimburse"
records the transfer with the guest's own id, and is disabled for a locked guest as it is for a
voter.

**After joining**: web `RedeemPage` and the overview inbox both navigate to the list after a
redeem; they pass a `joined` flag (query parameter) that `ExpenseListPage` consumes once:
if the list is a ledger with unclaimed guests, the chooser dialog opens. Android: `InviteJoiner`
navigates with the same flag and `ExpenseListScreen` opens the chooser. The multi-account
"Join with which account?" comes first, the guest chooser after the join. Dismissing is final
for that navigation; "This is me" on the list menu covers second thoughts.

**Rejections**: `guest_in_use`, `guest_claimed`, `guest_not_found`, `invalid_guest_name` get
rows in `web/src/i18n/apiErrors.ts`, Android's `ErrorText.kt` and the wire-contract error
table. `participant_frozen` on both clients names the participant through the label function,
so a locked guest reads "Dave: amounts locked" and a claimed one reads via the claimant.

**Strings** in all ten locales on both clients, paired by `crossClient.test.ts`.

**Android**: `ListGuest` next to `ListMember` in `:core`; `guestsJson` on `ListEntity` (Room
migration, with the `AppDbMigrationTest` workaround); `fold` and the alias map in
`ExpenseMath` (`:core`, no Android on the classpath); the five calls in `Api.kt`; the create
path in `ListsRepository` carries `guest_names`; any new class in the Koin modules.

**Gating**: every guest control, the create-dialog section and the chooser are shown only
when the account's `serverProtocol` is at or above the version below; against an older server
the ledger looks as it does today. Reading `guests` off a list object needs no gate (absent
means none).

## 9. Protocol

This is a protocol change: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 3 → 4, so the release that ships it is a major
one. A protocol-3 client receiving a guest id in an entry would render a live guest as a former
member and could not add one, and a claimed guest would appear as a stranger with a balance of
their own; that is the "cannot handle correctly" the versioning rule names. Both clients keep
`MIN_SERVER_PROTOCOL` where it is. Changelog row in `docs/wire-contract.md` "Protocol
version"; the three constants (`server/…/protocol.py`, `web/src/api/protocol.ts`, Android's
`Protocol.kt`) move together.

## 10. Not in this design

* Guests on shopping or checklist lists ("assigned to") — no.
* Server-wide or cross-list guests, guest contact details, a guest's own view of the ledger.
* Invites that name a guest.
* Merging two guests into one, or a guest into a *former* member.

## Implementation tickets

Filed as dependants of this ticket: shared cases (first, so both clients have a fixed target),
server, web, Android; then a release ticket when the maintainer asks.
title: Ledger guests: participants without an account — add, lock, claim on join (design)
